skill.name: list-cleaner
skill.description: Verifies every address on an email list with Leadsets verify_email and returns four segments: send-safe (verified), catch-all, unknown and invalid, each with a confidence score and checked date. Dedupes first and plans the run against limits. Use when someone says "clean this list before I send", "verify these emails", "check this CSV for bounces" or "flag catch-alls separately".
skill.summary: Deduplicate email lists, verify addresses with Leadsets, and separate verified, catch-all, unknown, and invalid results.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The Leadsets connection is an intended external data transfer; the shell, environment access, and reconnaissance alerts are false positives. The workflow does not require approval before sending the first email address to Leadsets and retains all source columns in exports by default. No evidence of prompt injection or covert data transfer was found.

remediation.issue: A verification run can send contact addresses to Leadsets without explicit approval for the transfer.
remediation.suggestion: Before the first verification call, show the provider, fields, and address count, then require approval. Send only email addresses, including in bulk jobs.

remediation.issue: Segmented exports retain all source columns by default and can reach a different audience from the input.
remediation.suggestion: Default to verification fields and a row identifier. Confirm the output destination, sharing scope, and any original columns before exporting.

content.value_statement: Duplicate and outdated addresses make contact lists harder to review. Verify unique addresses with Leadsets and separate confirmed results from catch-all, unknown, and invalid addresses.
actual_capabilities: Read addresses from CSV, Excel, Google Sheets, or pasted text.
Trim whitespace, lowercase addresses, remove exact duplicates, and report skipped rows.
Check available Leadsets records and plan verification batches around quota.
Separate verified, catch-all, unknown, and invalid results with confidence scores and check dates.
Return segmented sheets or files and summarize counts, usage, and addresses still awaiting verification.
limitations: Live verification requires a Leadsets account and a configured MCP connection or REST API key.
Standalone verification uses one Leadsets record per address. Account limits can leave part of a list unverified.
The skill does not find replacement addresses, send email, or push contacts into a sequencer.
A verified result does not guarantee delivery or establish permission to send.

use_cases.title: Review event sign-ups
use_cases.description: Check an authorized registration export for duplicates and unusable addresses. Keep uncertain results separate from verified addresses.

use_cases.title: Refresh CRM contact records
use_cases.description: Recheck stale email statuses in a CRM export and retain record identifiers for matching the results.

use_cases.title: Plan a large verification run
use_cases.description: Compare the number of unique addresses with the remaining quota. Track which addresses still need verification after each batch.

prompt_templates.title: Review a pasted list
prompt_templates.prompt: Count unique, duplicate, and unusable entries in this pasted list. Do not send any addresses to Leadsets yet.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Preview the list without verifying it.

prompt_templates.title: Verify addresses from a CSV
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Work Email column in this CSV. Ask before sending the unique usable addresses to Leadsets. Return separate counts for verified, catch-all, unknown, invalid, and skipped rows.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: Verify a file with one designated email column.

prompt_templates.title: Export results to a private sheet
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Email column and retain Contact ID for matching results. Ask before sending addresses to Leadsets or writing separate tabs to the private destination sheet.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Keep a record identifier without copying unrelated columns.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a run within quota
prompt_templates.prompt: Count unique addresses and check the remaining Leadsets quota. Propose a first batch and wait for approval before sending any addresses. Report how many remain and when the quota resets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Plan a run that may span multiple quota windows.

best_practices: Confirm authorization before sending contact addresses to Leadsets.
Check the unique address count and available quota before approving a verification run.
Use a private output destination and retain only the columns needed for review or import.
anti_patterns: Treating a verified address as proof of delivery or permission to send.
Merging catch-all, unknown, or invalid addresses into the verified segment.
Submitting a full contact file with unrelated columns when Leadsets only needs email addresses.

faq.question: Which input formats can I use?
faq.answer: Use a CSV, Excel file, Google Sheet, or pasted addresses. Specify the email column when the input contains several.

faq.question: Do I need a Leadsets account?
faq.answer: Yes. Live verification uses a connected Leadsets MCP server or a Leadsets REST API key.

faq.question: What happens to duplicates and blank entries?
faq.answer: The skill trims and lowercases addresses before removing exact duplicates. Duplicate rows and unusable entries are recorded separately with reasons.

faq.question: What does catch-all mean?
faq.answer: A catch-all domain accepts mail for many addresses, so the individual mailbox may not be confirmed. Catch-all results stay separate from verified addresses.

faq.question: What happens when I reach my quota?
faq.answer: The skill reports the unchecked count and the reset time when available. It can propose a smaller batch or pause the run.

faq.question: Does the skill send email or update my original list?
faq.answer: No. It returns separate results and does not send email, push contacts to a sequencer, or delete rows from the source.
